Head Start, the federal program providing free early education for low-income children, has benefited from strong bipartisan support since its 1965 inception, withstanding funding cuts and political turbulence across 11 presidencies.

But more recent threats from the second Trump administration have thrust Head Start into the spotlight. stories.headline: As Diesel Prices Soared, Arkansas District Saved With Electric School Buses
facts: Title: As Diesel Prices Soared, Arkansas District Saved With Electric School Buses

_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

Five years ago, diesel costs averaged $2.68 a gallon. This spring, that more than [doubled](https://gasprices.aaa.com/) to over $5.50. That’s not just a headline; it’s a real problem for anyone operating on a tight budget.

But for school districts, the issue is even more severe. The cost of fuel for just one school bus runs into thousands of dollars every year, and when diesel prices soar, school districts feel it in their budgets.

Electric school buses offer a solution. They can help districts save on fuel costs and insulate school budgets from the volatility of the global oil market. Here in Little Rock, we’re showing how this can work.
